correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md symmetry argument is valid for every linear isomorphism: averaging T^T T over the signed coordinate permutations preserves the same two-sided comparison and yields a scalar matrix. Hence the Euclidean circle is optimal. Sharp l_r extrema on the Euclidean circle occur at axes and diagonals; because p and q lie on the same side of 2, both summands attain their extrema in the same directions. This gives the two displayed ratios exactly, including p=q=2 and infinity endpoints. The equality with C_NJ matches the exact formulas in Mizuguchi--Saito Example 4.2.
